parole.testo: Internationalism, ultimately from French bureaucratie, likely transited through German Bürokratie. Compare also Yiddish ביוראָקראַטיע (byurokratye), Russian бюрократия (bjurokratija), Hungarian bürokrácia.

parole.significato: oxygen (the chemical element (symbol O) with an atomic number of 8 and relative atomic mass of 15.9994)
parole.testo: From ח־מ־ץ (kh-m-ts, “forming words relating to souring”) + ־ן (-n), ultimately calque of French oxygène via German Sauerstoff, a modern coinage from Ancient Greek ὀξύς (oxús, “sharp”) + γένος (génos, “birth”).

parole.significato: A brush: an implement used for brushing hair, scrubbing, or the like.
parole.testo: Coined by Eliezer Ben-Yehuda based upon French brosse, German Bürste, or English brush.
Borrowed from Western European languages, compare French thé and German Tee.
